title: Tenant assurance timeline and customer ask - July 29 2026
content:
TL;DR: We observed a regional inference degradation (EU-west) between 2026-07-29 02:10 and 2026-07-29 05:45 UTC that caused elevated latency and occasional truncated streaming responses for ~8% of active tenant sessions. Primary customer-facing impact: increased latency (500ms-2s above baseline) and ~0.3% rate of truncated streaming responses. No data was lost. Root cause: a cascading cache eviction combined with autoscaler oscillation for a subset of dedicated pools, which amplified queueing. We rolled a targeted restart of affected pools and applied an autoscaler fix; streaming truncation was mitigated by a temporary routing rule to healthy pools.

Summary for the status page (short, to post now):
- Incident: Regional inference degradation (EU-west) impacting latency and streaming stability
- Start: 2026-07-29 02:10 UTC
- Mitigation in place: 2026-07-29 04:00 UTC (partial routing to healthy pools); 2026-07-29 05:12 UTC (targeted restart and autoscaler patch)
- Current status: Service recovering; full validation running; customers on dedicated pools may see intermittent latency until 06:00 UTC
- Next update: 2026-07-29 06:00 UTC or earlier if status changes

Full customer-facing postmortem (concise, plain-language):
What happened
- Starting at ~02:10 UTC we saw a rise in queue length and token round-trip time for requests routed to several GPU pools in EU-west. This showed as higher latency and occasional truncated streaming responses for a small percentage of sessions.
- Investigation pointed to an unexpected cache eviction pattern in our KV prefix cache layer under a specific workload profile (many short-lived chat sessions with varied prompt prefixes). That eviction increased work per-request and changed resource utilization characteristics.
- The autoscaler reacted by rapidly scaling up and then down (oscillation) for a subset of dedicated pools due to a bug in our cooldown logic + a mis-read of transient load signals. That oscillation increased task churn and queueing for remaining healthy nodes.

Impact to customers
- Approx. 8% of active sessions in EU-west experienced >+500ms latency for multiple tokens; ~0.3% saw interrupted streaming responses that required client retry.
- Hosted API customers using regional routing to EU-west were affected; customers pinned to non-EU regions not impacted.
- No inference input or output logs were lost; audit logs and usage metering are intact.

What we did (timeline of actions)
- 02:10 UTC: Alerting triggered (queue depth and token latency anomaly)
- 02:17 UTC: Engineering on-call triaged; preliminary hypothesis around cache churn
- 02:42 UTC: Identified affected pools and isolated EV (eviction) metrics for KV caches
- 03:05 UTC: Deployed a temporary routing rule to divert a slice of traffic to healthy warm pools (reduced observed truncation)
- 04:00 UTC: Partial routing in effect; latency improved for many customers but still above SLO for some workloads
- 04:28 UTC: Confirmed autoscaler cooldown bug; prepared a hotfix
- 05:12 UTC: Rolled targeted restart of 6 affected GPU pools and applied autoscaler cooldown patch
- 05:45 UTC: Streaming truncation rate returned to baseline; latency approaching normal
- 06:00 UTC: Full recovery validation ongoing; monitoring dashboards show steady state

Customer-facing actions we recommend (what you can do now)
- If you experienced truncated streams, please retry the affected requests — our logs show retries succeed now.
- If you pinned a model/version to EU-west and can route to another region temporarily, consider setting a fallback region for non-sensitive workloads while we continue validation. Example: add a short failover in your client routing (priority list: eu-west -> us-east -> us-west).
- If you rely on low-latency streaming, you can (optionally) enable our conservative streaming buffer in client SDK v1.3.4 to smooth short-term jitter.

How we’ll prevent this from happening again (next steps and timeline)
- Short (done): autoscaler cooldown fix deployed; routing playbook updated to detect oscillation patterns faster (complete).
- Medium (2–3 weeks): introduce a protective throttle for KV cache eviction bursts to limit per-node work amplification; add synthetic load tests that emulate many short-lived chats (in planning, PR #2337).
- Long (1–3 months): larger autoscaler rewrite to make scaling decisions resilient to transient signals; improved per-pool health scoring and automatic fallback to healthy pools without full restart (roadmap item tracked in JIRA-OPS-411).

Verification & validation for customers (how we’ll prove this is fixed)
- We'll publish anonymized aggregated metrics for EU-west on the status page: queue depth, token RTT distribution, truncation rate (by 2026-08-05).
- For enterprise customers with dedicated pools, we can run a tenant-specific replay of a safe, redacted sample workload in a test slot and share the observed metrics (coordinate via your CSM).

Customer communication plan (what they’ll see)
- Status page: immediate short notice (this doc), update at 06:00 UTC with recovery confirmation, follow-up summary and aggregated metrics by 2026-08-05.
- Customers with impacted dedicated pools: targeted email + CSM outreach with tenant-specific evidence, and an offer to schedule a replay/validation window.

Open questions / internal notes to self (left here so CSMs know we’re still looking):
- Need to double-check whether a specific model family (decoder-only vs. encoder-decoder) disproportionately hit the eviction pattern — engineering to confirm by 2026-08-01.
- Verify if any customer-level traffic patterns (prompt sizes, session churn) correlate with higher impact; follow-up asks for customers: anonymized sample traces (we will redact).

Suggested statuspage snippets (short variations you can drop into page):
- Short: "We are investigating a regional inference degradation in EU-west affecting latency and streaming stability. Mitigations in progress. No user data lost."
- Mid: "Issue identified as cache eviction + autoscaler oscillation for subset of EU-west pools. Traffic partially rerouted while we apply fixes. Estimated full recovery: 06:00 UTC."
- Final/closure: "Service recovered. Root cause: KV cache eviction burst + autoscaler cooldown bug leading to task churn. Fixes deployed; we will publish aggregated metrics and next-step timeline by 2026-08-05."

Draft customer email (short):
Subject: Update: EU-west inference degradation (July 29) — recovery under way
Hi <CustomerName>,
We wanted to let you know we observed a regional inference degradation affecting some EU-west sessions this morning. We have implemented routing mitigations and deployed targeted fixes; streaming truncation and elevated latency have been addressed. We’re continuing validation and will share aggregated metrics and a concise post-incident summary by 2026-08-05. If you’d like us to run a tenant-specific replay in a safe test environment, reply to this email and we’ll coordinate.
Thanks — Priya (on behalf of Incident Ops)

Notes for handoff to CSM/SE:
- Attach JIRA-INC-1729 evidence bundle (logs + anonymized traces)
- Offer a replay window (slot duration 30–60 minutes) and the list of metrics we’ll return: per-token RTT, truncation count, queue depth
- If customer asks for credits or SLO adjustment: escalate to AUS (billing) if impact window > 3 hours or confirmed material customer business impact

Bottom-line for customers: we apologize for the disruption. We've fixed the immediate causes, we’re validating, and we will publish aggregated evidence and stronger protections soon.

---
Notes to internal reader: this doc is a working draft — keep phrasing conservative for public-facing copy (avoid 'bug' vs. 'issue' variance), coordinate final status page copy with comms@redwood and legal if any enterprise customers request formal statements.

(End of draft)
